title: Intersection Theory In One Map
notes: Open with the entire appendix in one sentence: divisors gave the familiar Riemann-Roch formulas on curves and surfaces, but higher dimension needs a graded language. The pipeline image is not decoration; it is the dependency order for the lecture. Cycles are raw data, rational equivalence permits movement, the Chow ring gives products, Chern classes put bundles into that ring, and HRR extracts a top-degree integer.

title: Why Divisors Are Not Enough
notes: Use this slide to slow down the first conceptual shift. Divisors are codimension-one objects, so they are only the first nontrivial layer of the Chow ring. On a surface, multiplying two divisor classes already reaches zero-cycles, which explains why the older surface theory looked purely numerical. In higher dimension, the product may be a curve class, a surface class, or another intermediate class before any degree can be taken.

title: Cycles And Rational Equivalence
notes: Define cycles as deliberately formal objects: the coefficients remember multiplicity and sign, while the symbols remember irreducible subvarieties of fixed codimension. Rational equivalence is the permission slip for movement. It is the reason intersection theory can ask for a representative that meets another cycle properly without changing the class being computed. Stress that this quotient is not a technical nuisance; it is the mechanism that makes products robust.

title: Push Pull And The Diagonal
notes: This slide is the bridge from cycles as generators to the Chow ring as a computational object. The diagonal is the conceptual trick: a product inside X is pulled back from an external product on X times X. Pushforward, pullback, and the projection formula are the compatibility checks that stop the construction from depending on accidental choices. The graph should be read as a proof dependency map rather than a taxonomy.

title: Local Multiplicity Needs Tor
notes: Use Tor as the first moment where the appendix reveals how much algebra is underneath the geometry. Students may know length from curve intersections on surfaces, so explain why that model is too optimistic in general. The alternating Tor formula is a compact way to say that intersection multiplicity is not just the size of one quotient; it is the Euler characteristic of a local derived tensor product. That is exactly the kind of correction needed for the Chow product to be well defined.

title: When Singularities Break The Rules
notes: This warning prevents a common overextension. The surface-looking picture of a cone is intentionally simple, because the point is not to solve a cone problem but to expose the role of hypotheses. Smoothness, proper intersection, and a usable moving lemma are doing real work in the Chow ring construction. When singularities enter, the local algebra and equivalence relations need different tools. That is why the appendix later treats singular Riemann-Roch as a separate generalization rather than a routine corollary.

title: The Chow Ring Of Projective Space
notes: Projective space is the smallest honest computational arena. The hyperplane class h generates all codimensions, multiplication adds exponents, and the relation h to the n plus one equals zero is simply the absence of classes past the dimension. Tie the table to the JSON check: in projective three-space, h to the fourth vanishes. This example prepares students for top-degree extraction, because h cubed is the class whose degree is one.

title: Properties That Make Computation Possible
notes: Present these properties as the reason Chow rings become usable rather than merely definitional. Picard identifies the old divisor language inside A one. Affine invariance says that adding irrelevant affine directions does not alter the group. Localization lets one compute by removing and replacing closed pieces. The projective bundle formula is the key that unlocks Chern classes, because it gives a controlled basis in which the tautological class satisfies a relation.

title: Chern Classes From Projective Bundles
notes: The projective bundle formula is the structural source of Chern classes in this appendix. The tautological class xi gives a basis up to xi to the r minus one, so xi to the r must be rewritten in that basis. The coefficients are the Chern classes. This is a good moment to contrast line bundles, where c one is enough, with higher-rank bundles, where the total polynomial records all codimension contributions.

title: Splitting Principle And Exact Sequences
notes: Treat the splitting principle as a temporary change of universe where computations are easier. Once the bundle is written as formal line-bundle roots, c sub t of E becomes a product of linear factors. Symmetric polynomials in the roots are honest Chern classes back on the original variety. The notebook check makes this concrete: for a rank-two piece and a line piece, the residual in the exact-sequence multiplicativity identity is exactly zero.

title: Top Chern And Self-Intersection
notes: This slide is the geometric payoff of Chern classes before Riemann-Roch appears. A generic section of a rank r bundle should vanish in codimension r, and the top Chern class records that zero locus. The self-intersection formula then says that pushing Y into X and pulling back again measures the top Chern class of the normal bundle. This is exactly the kind of mechanism used when the appendix computes constraints for surfaces in projective four-space.

title: Chern Character And Todd Class
notes: Pause on the formal roots. The roots are not extra geometry living on X; they are a computational fiction justified by the splitting principle. The Chern character and Todd class are symmetric power series in those roots, so they can be rewritten in Chern classes. The denominators explain why rational Chow groups appear. The important reassurance is that HRR will take the degree of the top component and return an integral Euler characteristic.

title: Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch
notes: Now the lecture reaches the promised endpoint. HRR says that an Euler characteristic, which is defined cohomologically, can be computed by multiplying characteristic classes and extracting the codimension-n part. The projective-plane ledger makes this executable: the saved rows for O of d match the binomial formula. The lab link is useful after lecture because students can vary d and see the top-degree computation remain polynomial.

title: Old Riemann-Roch Formulas Reappear
notes: Use this as the sanity check for the appendix. The curve formula and the surface formula should feel familiar from earlier chapters, while the surface-in-projective-four-space relation shows why the new machinery is stronger than nostalgia. The same HRR expression produces classical Riemann-Roch, explains the Todd correction, and combines with self-intersection to produce a numerical condition on embedded surfaces. This is where students should see the appendix as unification rather than a detour.

title: Complements And Exit Map
notes: Close by widening the map without pretending to prove the complements. Nakai-Moishezon says intersection numbers detect positivity. The Hodge index theorem adds a sign rule for middle-dimensional intersections under a primitivity condition. Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch makes HRR functorial by measuring how Chern character fails to commute with pushforward. Singular variants keep the same bookkeeping ambition but require new hypotheses and constructions. The final takeaway is that Appendix A builds the language used by these later branches.
